items.title: A single AI model simulates the behavior of many substances, from sliding sand to folding proteins
items.summary: Today, a scientist who wants to simulate a physical process must pick the right tool for that one job, such as a solver built for flowing water or another designed to model the way a protein folds. Typically, when scientists model materials and physical processes using Lagrangian particles, they use a governing equation that defines the fundamental laws which control how that material behaves over time and space.

items.title: TOMORI: A Tool-Orchestrated Mixing Operator for REAPER Interaction
items.summary: Code-based agents can operate creative software, but mixing requests often describe an intended sound without specifying the edits needed to achieve it. We present TOMORI, a code-based mixing-agent harness for native digital audio workstation (DAW) control. Custom plugins provide REAPER project inspection, optional audio measurement, and execution of model-generated Lua code.

items.title: Encoding of musical structures in hidden units of restricted Boltzmann machines
items.summary: Restricted Boltzmann machines (RBMs) are energy-based models originating from statistical physics. In this study, we investigate how musical structures are represented in the hidden layer of a Bernoulli-Bernoulli RBM trained on binary piano-roll representations of J.~S.~Bach's music.

items.title: Integrate the Reward, Don't Sample It: Window Likelihood for Interruptions and Backchannels in Full-Duplex Speech Models
items.summary: When a user talks over a full-duplex spoken dialogue model, the model must decide whether the user is interrupting (stop) or only backchannelling (carry on). The probability that the model stops inside a short window is a known function of a few stop probabilities that the policy itself emits, yet GRPO estimates it by sampling.

items.title: REAL-2MIX: Evaluating Identity Faithfulness in Audio-Visual Target Speaker Extraction
items.summary: Audio-visual target speaker extraction should recover the person indicated by the video, rather than repeatedly return the acoustically dominant voice. Its 77 scenes contain 7,598 clips; filtering yields 6,038 evaluable mixtures, each queried for both speakers, giving 12,076 paired target queries.

items.title: Bridging Spiking and Continuous Dynamics in Spiking Neural Networks: A Muscle-Inspired Model
items.summary: Transforming the spike trains produced by spiking neural networks (SNNs) into continuous signals through biologically inspired mechanisms remains an open challenge in generative and regression tasks. Our approach uses second-order dynamics to model the temporal integration of spiking activity.

items.title: SPDMX: Large-Scale Open Stem Audio From Symbolic Music
items.summary: Large public datasets have driven recent progress in machine learning, from text and vision to speech and general audio. Music remains an outlier, as copyright blocks redistribution of training audio, while many modern tasks need individual stems rather than mixtures.

items.title: AircraftWitness: How Often Aircraft Can Locate Recordings
items.summary: The best of three locators places clear-pass clips within 1 km at 4 places, where a uniform guess predicts 0.57 (p = 0.0065 after correcting for the pick). On 360 clips from 7 places of a GPS-timed network, two locators place 6% and 8% within 1 km. On 1,600 random public recordings, picked and cut without the truth in a time-bounded run, the three locators answer at most 20 times and place at most 2.

items.title: NAVE: A Normalized, Adaptive Conformer for Antarctic Whale Vocalization Detection
items.summary: Antarctic whale vocalization detection requires temporally localizing call boundaries in long underwater recordings and classifying them into predefined call types. These difficulties are further amplified by time-varying noise that can mask whale calls and by site-specific ambient sound characteristics to which a trained model may not generalize.

items.title: AISHELL8-FISHEYE: A Fisheye Audio-Visual Dataset for Target Speaker Extraction with Distortion-Aware Baselines
items.summary: Fisheye cameras offer wide visual coverage but distort facial and lip geometry, challenging audio-visual target speaker extraction. We introduce AISHELL8-FISHEYE, a 47.03-hour corpus of 94 Mandarin speakers with synchronized audio and paired fisheye and normal-camera videos.

items.title: GTCRN-SS: Lightweight Causal Speech Separation with Residual Allocation and Reconstruction Refinement
items.summary: Low-complexity causal speech separation must preserve speaker information and allocate residual mixture energy without relying on future feature frames. We present GTCRN-SS, a two-stage time-frequency separator that adapts the compact GTCRN enhancement backbone to fixed-output speech separation. These results establish GTCRN-SS as an effective quality-efficiency operating point for causal monaural speech separation.

items.title: AccentCanvas: Activity-Guided Bidirectional Accent Conversion
items.summary: Accent conversion for dubbing must change pronunciation while preserving content, voice, and source timing. We present AccentCanvas, a shared discrete diffusion model for normalization and L1-to-L2 conversion, trained on cross-paired shared-prompt recordings and synthetic pairs.

items.title: Conflict-Aware Meta-Learning for Generalizable Speech Deepfake Detection
items.summary: Speech deepfake detectors built on large self-supervised learning front-ends achieve high in-domain accuracy, yet suffer degradation under domain shift caused by unseen synthesizers, transmission codecs, or unfamiliar acoustic conditions. Meta-learning, particularly model-agnostic meta-learning for domain generalization (MLDG), addresses this issue by simulating domain shifts.

items.title: Polarization calibration of fisheye cameras using skylight in the wild
items.summary: Skylight polarization provides directional cues for robotic navigation, but fisheye lens effects and analyzer imperfections can degrade polarization measurements across the field of view. Given known geometric calibration, rotations between camera frames can be estimated using visual features and cross-frame directional polarized light consistency can be used for polarization calibration.

items.title: FATHOM: World-Model-Guided Diffusion Action-Trajectory Selection for Sparse-Marker AUV Tracking
items.summary: Reliable relative tracking is fundamental to cooperative autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), yet remains challenging under nonlinear vehicle dynamics and degraded underwater visual conditions. To address the resulting partial-observation control problem, this paper proposes FATHOM, a world-model-guided diffusion action-trajectory selection framework for sparse-marker AUV tracking.

items.title: Localizing and Editing the Goal Representation of a Vision-Language-Action Model
items.summary: Activation patching shows that the first action depends mostly on the instruction tokens before layer 12 and on the last prompt token from layer 16 onward. From layer 16, only patches at every decoded action token redirected the robot (15 of 18 rollouts at layer 24). Goal edits in OpenVLA should act before layer 12 or patch every action token.

items.title: Lodos: A Lightweight Simulator Designed for Contact-Rich Interactions with Detailed Meshes
items.summary: In recent years, massively parallelized rigid-body simulation has played a central role in robotics research, enabling rapid progress in areas such as reinforcement learning, stochastic optimal control, and randomized smoothing-based trajectory optimization.

items.title: Lodos-v2: An Efficient Primal Formulation of the Exact Frictional Contact Problem
items.summary: Lodos-v2 is a GPU-based simulation framework for massively parallel rigid-body dynamics with contact. First, it introduces an efficient algorithm for solving the exact frictional contact problem by sequentially solving a cascade of convex relaxations in primal form within an outer proximal minimization loop.

items.title: What Limits mmWave Human-State Sensing for Robot Perception?
items.summary: Assistive robots and search-and-rescue platforms require reliable human state sensing in smoke, darkness, and privacy-sensitive environments, where cameras and LiDAR may be unreliable Millimeter-wave radar offers an alternative that works without ambient light, penetrates smoke, and does not capture visual appearance.

items.title: STRIDE: Learning Humanoid Locomotion in Minutes with Acceleration-Based Rewards
items.summary: Learning locomotion directly on a humanoid robot is a promising direction to avoid the sim-to-real gap. However, locomotion rewards in Reinforcement Learning (RL) typically track the base velocity, which cannot be measured onboard without an external motion capture system or well-calibrated state estimator.

items.title: ActPrune: Action-Grounded Visual Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models perform versatile manipulation tasks from language instructions, but their inference cost limits how fast a robot can respond in closed-loop control. Visual token pruning reduces this cost; however, prior methods estimate token redundancy from encoded visual embeddings or attention, only after the visual encoder has processed the entire observation.

items.title: It Takes Two to Tangram: Multi-Agent Object Centric Reinforcement Learning for Assembly
items.summary: Geometric assembly requires fine spatiotemporal coordination to place parts without causing collisions or deadlocks under tight clearances. To address this, we present an object-centric reinforcement learning framework that treats each part as an agent and learns a shared policy for continuous assembly control.

items.title: VICTR: Value-Informed In-Context Learning for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Recent advances in robot foundation models have highlighted the potential of in-context learning (ICL) for adapting robot behavior from demonstrations without further fine-tuning. We introduce VICTR, a framework enabling in-context learning in VLAs via progress-informed context retrieval built around an In-Context Value Function Estimator (IC-VFE).

items.title: National and State-Level Approaches to Automated Vehicle Certification: A Comparative Framework for State Operational Governance
items.summary: Automated vehicle (AV) deployment in the United States is expanding without a unified federal certification framework, leading to substantial variation in how states authorize and oversee AV testing and deployment. This paper examines how U.S.

items.title: ForPC: Force-Aware Whole-Body Control for Precise Humanoid Cart Pushing
items.summary: Humanoid robots are expected to take over strenuous material handling in manufacturing, logistics, and healthcare, where operating existing wheeled carts would let them move heavy loads without modifying the workplace.

items.title: CS-Pi: Constraint-Satisfying Flow Policy Sampling
items.summary: A flow-matching policy deployed in the field must often satisfy a constraint that was absent from its demonstrations, such as avoiding an obstacle it has never seen. Enforcing it must not discard what the policy learned: an action the policy would rarely sample may avoid the obstacle yet fail the task.

items.title: Meituan-Robotics-0: A Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Desktop Manipulation
items.summary: We present Meituan-Robotics-0 (MR0), a vision-language-action foundation model and embodied-agent system for stationary-base desktop manipulation. An event-driven agent maintains persistent task events and reassesses plans when progress or feasibility changes, enabling cross-task retrieval and conditional task resumption.

items.title: Q-OIL: Optimistic Exploration in Learning from Human Interventions
items.summary: However, studying human-in-the-loop robot learning is difficult: real-world experiments are slow and expensive, so most algorithm development relies on simulated human models. Building on these insights, we propose Q-OIL, a method that adds optimistic bonuses to intervention transitions in reinforcement learning and softly guides exploration toward human corrections.

items.title: Benchmarking Machine Learning for Chaotic Three-Body Dynamics in Astrophysics
items.summary: We explore a hierarchy of prediction problems stemming from chaotic three-body systems and benchmark existing ML approaches, including general-purpose prediction algorithms and those that build on top of foundational physics models. We then design a hierarchy of learning tasks, focusing mainly on two broad problems: stability prediction and trajectory prediction.

items.title: Not All Misalignment Is Alike: A Decomposed Benchmark for Emergent Misalignment
items.summary: Emergent misalignment (EM), in which fine-tuning on a narrow task induces misaligned behaviour on unrelated prompts, has been demonstrated across a wide range of datasets, model families, and training setups. These evaluations can also conflate misalignment with capability loss and offer little insight into the specific ways misalignment manifests.

items.title: PINNeval: A Comprehensive Evaluation Standard for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
items.summary: The Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) literature has produced a rapidly expanding catalogue of methods. We divide a PINN training pipeline systematically into four components and observe that many existing benchmarks study these components in isolation. These components are domain-importance adaptation, loss balancing, neural network architecture, and optimization scheme.

items.title: Minimum-Sufficient Knowledge and Computation for Wind Energy Predictive Analysis
items.summary: As proof of concept, we isolate adaptive knowledge routing, the decision underlying Knowledge-Guided Machine Learning (KGML), which conventionally injects external knowledge unconditionally rather than only where needed.

items.title: How Small Can We Go? Calibrating Activation-Cache Compression for SAE Training
items.summary: To train a sparse autoencoder (SAE), you need a massive cache of model activations. We found that in the retraining test, there is no clear scale for retained features. On a GPT-2 cache, rounding everything to fp16 keeps 60.6% of features, but changing one value in a million by the smallest step fp32 allows (a change eight orders of magnitude smaller) keeps only 70.5%.

items.title: Evolutionary Adaptive Metric Learning: A Multi-Objective Framework for Learning Local Distance Functions in Nearest Neighbor Classification
items.summary: We propose EAML (Evolutionary Adaptive Metric Learning), a framework that learns instance-dependent positive-definite metrics through a low-dimensional parameterization. Experiments on synthetic data with region-dependent feature relevance show that EAML can recover local metric variations and outperform global metrics.

items.title: What Are LLM Agents Actually Learning on Low-Budget Molecular Optimization Benchmarks?
items.summary: Recent work reports large gains for LLM agents on low-budget molecular optimization. On PMO at 50 oracle calls, a GPT-4o mini agent's sum AUC falls from 14.44 to 4.85 after task names and curated reference compounds are hidden.

items.title: Interpretable Multifidelity Learning with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Spatiotemporal Nuclear Reactor Flow Modeling
items.summary: High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of nuclear reactor systems are computationally expensive, motivating machine learning methods that reduce cost while preserving accuracy. Multifidelity surrogate modeling addresses this by combining inexpensive low-fidelity data with limited high-fidelity data.

items.title: Does Country Matter? Evaluating Geographic Sensitivity of Large Language Models in Zero-Shot Chronic Kidney Disease Screening
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) show strong zero-shot reasoning capabilities, yet their sensitivity to prompt context raises questions about reliability in deployment. This study investigates whether geographic context embedded in prompts influences LLM-based chronic kidney disease (CKD) screening, independent of any change in patient features.

items.title: Emergent Low-Dimensional Topological Dynamics Dictate Generalization and Escape Mechanics in Billion-Parameter Neural Networks
items.summary: The remarkable generalization of modern over-parameterized neural networks defies classical statistical learning bounds. By equipping the parameter space with a regularized Hessian metric $g_{ij} = \nabla_i \nabla_j L + \epsilon \delta_{ij}$ and analyzing stochastic Langevin diffusion on loss sublevel sets, we derive a rigorous Topological Generalization Bound grounded in projected subspace persistent homology.

items.title: Adaptive Depth Aggregation in Graph Transformers for Long-Range Graph Reasoning
items.summary: Graph Transformers improve long-range node-to-node communication through global or structure-aware interactions. To study this hypothesis, we formalize Graph Transformer residual computation as a causal node-wise history of graph-propagation and feed-forward network (FFN) contributions, making depth aggregation an explicit interface choice.

items.title: Generative Reconstruction of Full-Field Sensor States for Safety-Critical Digital Twins
items.summary: Accurate reconstruction of incomplete sensor fields is critical for state awareness in safety-critical digital twins (DTs). For intra-experiment reconstruction within the PG{-}29 depressurized conduction cooldown (DCC) test, the models combine graph-based spatial encoding with gated recurrent units.

items.title: Rethinking Data Selection as Distribution Matching on Semantic Manifolds
items.summary: Instruction tuning of large language models and large vision language models relies on massive training data, which incurs substantial computational and storage costs. We propose QMAC, a quality aware multiband characteristic function matching method that formulates data selection as a joint optimization problem of distribution matching and quality filtering.

items.title: Embedding Consistent Recurrent Neural Networks in Finite Element Simulations for Path-Dependent Damage Prediction
items.summary: Capturing sheet-metal localisation physics with a trained surrogate inside a finite element (FEM) solver requires the surrogate to deliver consistent predictions irrespective of the solver's strain-increment count, which is difficult to control in non-linear explicit codes.

items.title: FasterRW: An Efficient Prior-Assisted Random Walk Solver for Thermal Analysis
items.summary: Feynman--Kac random walk methods can estimate localized temperatures without solving the global field, but in practical settings without Dirichlet boundaries they require very long paths to control the truncation residual. This paper presents FasterRW, a continuation-value framework for accelerating Feynman--Kac thermal random walks.

items.title: Jacobian-Causal Memory Control for Persistent Memory in Language Model Systems
items.summary: Persistent-memory systems choose not only which records are retrieved but which prior information can alter current inference. Under explicit smoothness and bounded-estimation assumptions, we prove a quadratic local-approximation bound, characterize the target effects reachable by a set of signatures, bound selection regret under signature error, and bound non-additive interactions between simultaneous memories.

items.title: Debate to Deceive: Poisoning LLM's Fact-Checking via Game-Theoretic Multi-Agent Debate
items.summary: Knowledge attacks on Large Language Models, such as manipulating fact-checking judgments, pose significant risks to AI reliability. Existing approaches -- adversarial suffix/template injection and single-agent self-reflection -- lack robustness across diverse defenses and are prone to confirmation bias and costly trial-and-error, respectively.

items.title: AttentionSwitch: Jailbreak Defense for LLMs via Joint Learning of Sparse Attention-Head Selection and Scaling
items.summary: Large language models have achieved remarkable performance across a wide range of tasks, yet they remain susceptible to jailbreak attacks that circumvent safety mechanisms and elicit harmful or unintended outputs. In this work, we introduce AttentionSwitch, the first jailbreak defense to jointly optimize intervention sites and strengths within a frozen LLM.

items.title: AlterNet: Adaptive-Depth Mixture-of-Experts with Learned Halting for Elastic Inference
items.summary: We propose a novel architecture that combines the Mixture-of-Experts architecture with shallow experts and a novel dynamic-depth system to make the extent of a forward pass dynamically adjustable.

items.title: Memory-Aware Multi-Agent Architecture with LLM-based Orchestration for Conversational Recommendation
items.summary: Conversational recommender systems often treat user sessions in isolation, limiting their ability to capture how user intent evolves over time. In this work, we propose a memory-aware multi-agent architecture for conversational recommendation, in which LLMs act as orchestration layers that coordinate intent refinement, query construction, and interaction flow.

items.title: Cancellation Is Not Enough: What Retries Leave Behind in an Overloaded LLM Engine
items.summary: Clients and proxies in front of an LLM engine retry calls that time out. After a transient overload, these retries can keep the engine from recovering even when calls arrive below its capacity. We find that with retries on, cancellation alone did not restore service in any run, and only 12-38% of the calls that arrived after the overload were delivered.

items.title: Transporting the Past: An Optimal Transport View of Backtracking Counterfactuals
items.summary: We study backtracking counterfactual inference for Structural Causal Models (SCMs) through the lens of optimal transport. In SCMs, a factual observation generally induces a posterior distribution over exogenous variables, making counterfactual inference inherently distributional.

items.title: ChainFlow: Few-Step Latent Flow Matching for Speculative Decoding
items.summary: Speculative decoding has become a standard way to accelerate LLM inference: a lightweight drafter proposes tokens that the target verifies in one parallel pass.

items.title: Pdb or Not to Be: Comparing Debugging Interfaces With Pass$_{X}$@$k$
items.summary: Interactive debuggers are indispensable to human software development, yet coding agents overwhelmingly rely on edit-execute-observe loops, using common bash tools, test scripts, and print statements to debug via repeated shell commands.

items.title: IWIBench: Evaluating Gradient-Free Model Driven Intra-weight Injection
items.summary: Intra-weight injection lets one model change another model's behaviour by editing its weights directly, without gradients. We introduce IWIBench, which measures a large editor model's ability to modify the weights of a smaller target model (typically Gemma 3 4B IT) to achieve one of ten classical text-editing objectives while preserving its other capabilities.

items.title: Decision Context: Persistent Behavioral Learning for AI Agents
items.summary: LLM agents do not learn from corrections across sessions. We present Forge Decision Context (forge_dc), a system that captures behavioral signals from human corrections and self-assessed tool-call failures, compiles them into imperative RULE directives, and injects them at the decision points where they apply.

items.title: Aspect-wise Pairwise Tournaments for Test-Time Selection
items.summary: Here we introduce Aspect-wise Pairwise Tournaments (APT), which verifies by comparison and compares by aspect. We find that both components matter; neither binary approval over the same aspects nor a generic pairwise judge at a matched budget matches APT.

items.summary: E-commerce supply chains generate large volumes of customer feedback and operational data that remain underutilized in inventory management.

items.title: NormGym: Evaluating Normative Competence through Social Interaction
items.summary: Normative competence, the ability to infer socially enforced expectations from interaction and adjust behavior accordingly, is essential for agents operating in unfamiliar human communities. Yet existing evaluations largely test whether agents can recognize or apply norms they may already know, rather than whether they can acquire previously unknown norms from social interaction.
